reply:
I can't verify any such judgment, so I won't give you one. Quoting a judgment that turns out to be wrong or made up could hurt your case and your credibility. I don't cite court cases at all; only a lawyer who has read the actual judgment should do that.

What you can safely do in your notice:
- Ask for the deposit plus interest from the date it was due. Whether interest is awarded, and at what rate, is for the court to decide.
- Rely on your rent agreement. Not returning a deposit when the agreement says it is refundable is a breach of contract, for which compensation can be claimed under the Indian Contract Act, 1872, Section 73.

If you want a judgment quoted, a lawyer or the free legal aid service (call 15100) can find and check one. Shall I draft a notice without it?
